analysis.detail: The advisory concerns pac4j's own CSRF protection: CsrfAuthorizer and DefaultCsrfTokenGenerator compare tokens through String.hashCode(), so a collision defeats the check. Those classes are reached only through pac4j's security engine (SecurityLogic / CallbackLogic, via DefaultAuthorizationChecker and DefaultMatchingChecker). This module never enters that engine: it drives SAML2Client directly (SAML2Filter#getRedirectionAction and #getCredentials) and configures no authorizer or matcher. A bytecode scan of the shipped bundle confirms that org.pac4j.core.authorization.authorizer.CsrfAuthorizer and org.pac4j.core.matching.matcher.csrf.* are referenced by no class outside pac4j-core itself, and by none of the module's own classes. Cross-site forgery on the assertion consumer endpoint is handled by SAML RelayState, not by a pac4j CSRF token. No fix exists in the pac4j 4.x line: the advisory is fixed in 5.7.10 and 6.4.1, and pac4j-saml-opensamlv3 - the OpenSAML 3 binding this module depends on - was last published as 4.5.10. Remediation therefore means migrating to pac4j-saml 5.7.11 on OpenSAML 4, tracked separately.
